sections.title: Why this module matters
sections.body: Spring Core interview questions test whether you understand the framework underneath Spring Boot — the IoC container, dependency injection (constructor vs setter vs field), bean lifecycles and scopes, the BeanFactory vs ApplicationContext, AOP fundamentals (proxies, advices, pointcuts), and the @Transactional internals interviewers love to probe. This page covers the conceptual layer that lets you debug a real Spring app instead of just write one. Pair this page with the Spring Boot page (auto-configuration, starters, profiles), Spring Data JPA / Hibernate, Spring Security, Spring WebFlux, and Spring Batch.

sections.title: Mental model
sections.body:
Spring Core in three layers:

1. **IoC container** — `BeanDefinition` → `BeanFactory` → `ApplicationContext`.
2. **Lifecycle** — instantiate → populate → aware → BPP-before → `@PostConstruct` → BPP-after → ready.
3. **Cross-cutting** — AOP proxies (JDK or CGLIB), `@Transactional`, events.

Senior questions probe the **proxy boundary**: same-bean self-invocation skips the aspect; this is where 80% of `@Transactional` bugs live.

sections.title: Must-know concepts
sections.body:
The interview surface for this module breaks into these focus areas:

- **Aop** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Bean lifecycle** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Comparisons** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Custom components** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Dependency injection** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Spring events** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Spring internals** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Scenario-based** — applied questions tying multiple topics together. Drill these *last*, after the fundamentals are sharp.

sections.title: Likely interview hooks
sections.body:
- **Constructor injection** > setter > field — *because* `final`, fail-fast cycles, easy testing.
- **`@Transactional` self-invocation** doesn't go through the proxy — readiness fact.
- **`@Configuration` proxyBeanMethods** — true → CGLIB, inter-`@Bean` calls return singletons; false → faster start, no inter-call guarantee.
- **Circular deps** — constructor cycles fail fast; setter cycles use **early references**.
- **`@Primary` vs `@Qualifier`** — default vs explicit disambiguation.

sections.title: Speaking template
sections.body: > *"I'd register this as a `@Component` / `@Configuration` `@Bean`, prefer constructor injection so <reason>, and apply <`@Transactional` / `@Async` / aspect> via the proxy — knowing the proxy boundary means I'd avoid same-bean self-invocation and split the responsibility into <bean A> + <bean B>."*
